stem:
Meena wants to find out whether the temperature of water affects how quickly sugar dissolves.

She plans two trials in her kitchen at home.

Which row shows a fair test?

options.text: Trial 1: 40 g sugar, 100 cm³ water at 30 °C; Trial 2: 40 g sugar, 100 cm³ water at 60 °C
Trial 1: 40 g sugar, 100 cm³ water at 30 °C; Trial 2: 60 g sugar, 100 cm³ water at 60 °C
Trial 1: 40 g sugar, 100 cm³ water at 60 °C; Trial 2: 40 g sugar, 150 cm³ water at 60 °C
Trial 1: 40 g sugar, 100 cm³ water at 30 °C, stirred; Trial 2: 40 g sugar, 100 cm³ water at 60 °C, not stirred

tables: {"headers":["Trial 1","Trial 2"],"rows":[["40 g sugar, 100 cm³ water at 30 °C","40 g sugar, 100 cm³ water at 60 °C"],["40 g sugar, 100 cm³ water at 30 °C","60 g sugar, 100 cm³ water at 60 °C"],["40 g sugar, 100 cm³ water at 60 °C","40 g sugar, 150 cm³ water at 60 °C"],["40 g sugar, 100 cm³ water at 30 °C, stirred","40 g sugar, 100 cm³ water at 60 °C, not stirred"]],"row_labels":["A","B","C","D"],"caption":"","is_option_table":true}

teacher.key_rationale: A fair test of water temperature changes only the temperature while keeping the mass of sugar, the volume of water, and the stirring the same; only row A does this. Rows B, C and D each change a second condition (sugar mass, water volume, or stirring) or fail to test temperature at all.
